newsitem.title: GERMANY: Rexrodt says EMU to start on time, with Germany.
newsitem.headline: Rexrodt says EMU to start on time, with Germany.

text.p: German Economics Minister Guenter Rexrodt said on Monday that businesses should expect European economic and monetary union to begin punctually at the start of 1999.
And, brushing off Eurosceptics and pessimists, he also said Germany would qualify for the single currency's starting lineup.

"We can and will achieve the Maastricht criteria, and thus ensure that Europe does not miss this historic chance," he said in extracts from a statement he was due to give in a debate at the Hanover industry fair. German Finance Minister Theo Waigel has made it clear that he would insist on would-be EMU participants achieving a budget deficit this year of no more than 3.0 percent.

The Maastricht Treaty sets a target limit of three percent but qualifies this reference value, which has given rise to speculation that countries might be admitted which overshoot the limit after the decimal point.

Rexrodt said his ministry would issue a guide to businesses later this month on how to make the practical transition from accounting in marks to doing business in euros -- especially for the three-year transition before cash euros are used.
He said companies should be assisted if they wanted to switch their business into euros at the earliest opportunity.
